This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short), has been filed by the appellant-claimant being NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 22.03.2019 passed in MVC No.159/2017 by the Court of Prl. District Judge & MACT, Raichur,
(hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
3.

sentences.text:
The facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 29.03.2016 the injured petitioner Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy was proceeding as a pillion rider on TVS motorcycle Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/
2 bearing registration No.MH-12/DP-6913 and the vehicle was ridden by one Govind Rathod, who was in search of his missing son.

entities.text: Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When the said rider was riding the motorcycle in a very cautious manner at moderate speed on Manvi-Raichur main road, near Kapagal Village, Channabasaveshwar Petrol Bunk, due to negligent parking lorry bearing registration No.KA-36/4442 on the middle of the road by its driver respondent No.1 without any indication and without taking any precautionary measures, and due to NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB darkness, the rider of the motorcycle hit the parked lorry from back side.
As a result of which, they fell and sustained grievous injuries.

Govind Rathod the rider of the vehicle died in the Government Hospital, Manvi and injured initially took treatment at Government Hospital, Manvi and thereafter he was shifted to Basava Hospital,
Raichur.
The petitioner was shifted to Yashoda Hospital, Hyderabad and was admitted an inpatient in the said hospital from 30.03.2016 to 09.04.2016.

Later, he admitted to St.Mary's Hospital,
Bellary for follow up treatment.
It is stated that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 41 years, doing agriculture work and earning Rs.15,000/-.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been permanently disabled and lost source of income, causing dent to him financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
4. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not appear, hence they were placed ex-parte.
The NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB respondent No.3 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim petition and sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

6. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, next friend of petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and also examined one Doctor as PW.2 and got marked 82 documents as Exs.P1 to P82.

On the other hand, respondent No.2-Insurer examined its official as RW.1 and got marked four documents as Exs.R1 to R4.
7.

The Tribunal, after recording the evidence and considering the material on record, allowed the petition in part with costs and awarded compensation of Rs.7,45,880/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition until realization.
The tribunal also fastened contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner to an extent of 50%.

Being dissatisfied with the NC:
2024:KHC-K:9587-DB compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount and also questioning the contributory negligence of 50% fastened on the claimant/petitioner.
8. We have heard the learned counsel for appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.3- Insurance Company.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-petitioner that the Tribunal has erred in awarding inadequate compensation despite placing on record relevant documents regarding the permanent disability.

He further submits that the Tribunal has grossly erred in holding that both the driver of the offending vehicle and rider of the motorcycle have contributed 50% each for the cause of accident, even though the entire negligence is on the driver of Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/
3 the offending vehicle and NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB seeks indulgence of the Court, so also to enhance the compensation.

entities.text: Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, he would submit that the Insurance Company had preferred an appeal against the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.261/2016 arising out of the same accident, wherein the Tribunal has clearly held that though the charge sheet was filed against the deceased, no trial is conducted and case was abated in view of the fact that the rider-Govinda Rathod died.
Considering the material placed before the Tribunal, it is held that the accident occurred due to negligent parking of the lorry bearing No.KA-36/4442 by its driver.

The said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal was challenged by the Insurance Company before this Court in MFA No.201020/2017 and the same came to be dismissed by the learned Single Judge vide order dated 09.03.2021.
The Insurance Company has not challenged the same.
To substantiate his arguments, he produced the copy of the judgment passed by the learned Single Judge in MFA No.201020/2017.
On these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.

To fortify his submissions, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB learned Counsel has relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohammed Siddique and Another Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd.

And Others reported in 2020 Kant MAC 338 (SC).
10.
Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company supports the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, contending that the same does not call for any interference.

Further, he has not disputed the judgment dated 09.03.2021 passed by the learned Single Judge in MFA No.201020/2017 dismissing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company, which was also arising out of the same accident and the same is not challenged.
11. We have perused the records and considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.

Having heard the arguments on both sides, the points that arises for our consideration are;
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB (i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in fastening the liability of the Insurance Company only to the extent of 50%?
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?

(iii) What order or award?
12.
(iii) Point No.3: As per final order.

Regarding Point No.1:

sentences.text: We have examined the material placed before this Court.
The accident in question and the injuries suffered in the accident is not disputed between the parties.
Now the question is, whether the accident occurred due to negligent act on the part of the driver of the lorry, as well as the rider of the motorcycle who died in the accident.

In this regard, the complaint filed by Smt.Gangamma makes it clear that Manvi police have - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB registered the case in Crime No.83/2016 for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338, 283, 304-A of IPC and 187 of Motor Vehicles Act, against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.MH-12/DP-6913 and the driver of the lorry (name and address not known) bearing No.KA- 36/4442 and submitted the FIR to the Court.
Thereafter, the police visited the spot and conducted spot panchanama, prepared rough sketch, obtained M.V. report, recorded the statement of witnesses.

On completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer submitted abated charge sheet against accused No.1 for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338, 304A of IPC and filed charge sheet against accused No.2, the driver of the lorry for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 283 IPC and 187 of MV Act.

14. PW.1-Smt.Shantamma, the wife of the complainant deposed in her evidence that on the date of accident, the rider Govind Rathod was riding the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB motorcycle in a moderate speed by observing all the traffic rules by the extreme left side on Manvi-Raichur Main Road, near Channabasaveshwara Petrol Bunk of Kapgal village at about 19.30 hours, at that time, the respondent No.1 had parked the lorry in the middle of the road in a negligent manner without taking any precautionary measures and indicators.

As such,
due to darkness, the rider dashed to the said lorry to the back side, the impact of which, the rider and her husband both fell and sustained grievous injuries and the rider Govind Rathod succumbed to the injuries at Government Hospital, Manvi.

15. RW1-Krishna Vadaki, deposed in his evidence that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle as he was carrying two pillions which is in violation of Section 128 of M.V. Act.
However, during the cross-examination, he has clearly admitted that he is not an eye-witness to the accident and he is not personally acquainted with the facts of the case.

Considering the evidence from both sides, the Tribunal has - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB held that the rider of the motorcycle was himself negligent by taking two pillion riders without wearing helmet violating the provisions of law and to that extent he has contributed to the accident and hence equally the rider of the motorcycle and driver of the lorry were responsible.
Accordingly, the Tribunal has fixed contributory negligence in the ratio of 50:50 on the rider and driver of motorcycle and lorry, respectively.

Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/
5 16.

entities.text: Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have gone through the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohammed Siddique (supra), wherein it is observed that the rider of the motorcycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence and at the most it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of law.

Section 128 of M.V. Act,
1988, imposes a restriction on the rider of the motorcycle, not to carry more than one person on the motorcycle.
Section 194C of the Act inserted by the Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB violation of safety measures for motorcycle drivers and pillion riders.
Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more pillion rider, may be a violation of the law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more,
cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence, unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.

17. In the case on hand, the Tribunal has fastened the liability only to the extent of 50% on the driver of the lorry on the ground that the rider (deceased) of the motorcycle was carrying two pillions on the motorcycle by committing the offence punishable under Section 128 of M.V. Act.
In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court referred to supra, the finding of the Tribunal cannot be accepted.

18. Additionally, the Insurance Company has preferred the appeal against the judgment and award - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.261/2016 arising out the same accident, wherein the Tribunal has held that the accident occurred due to sole negligent act on the part of the driver of the lorry, which judgment was challenged by the Insurance Company before this Court in MFA No.201020/2017 which Appeal came to be dismissed and the same is not challenged.
In the instant case, the driver of the lorry has not taken any precautionary measures before parking the lorry in the middle of the road.
Even the owner or the lorry has not explained anything with regard to parking of the lorry in the middle of the road without following the Traffic Rules and Regulations.
19. In this regard, it is pertinent to mention about provisions of Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.

Rule of the Rules reads thus;
"Rule 15 Parking of the Vehicle (1) Every driver of a motor vehicle parking on any road shall park in such a way that it does not cause or is not likely to cause danger,
obstruction or undue inconvenience to other road users and the manner of parking is indicated by Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/
6 - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB any sign board or markings on the roadside, he shall park his vehicle in such manner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A plain reading of Rule 15(2)(iv) & (x) of Road Regulations, 1989 makes it clear that driver of a motor vehicle shall not park his vehicle on the main road or one carrying fast traffic or where parking is prohibited.

This Court, in the decision reported in 2019(2) T.A.C.282 (Kar) in the case of Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance company limited vs Savita & others, has dealt with similar kind of case, wherein abated charge sheet was filed against the deceased who dashed to parked truck.

At paragraph 10 of the Judgment, it is held as under :-

The accident is not in dispute.

The only question which is raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that abated charge sheet has been filed against the Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/
7 deceased and the deceased has also contributed to the alleged accident.

entities.text: Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would further contend that the lorry was parked on its right side by following the traffic rules as such, liability ought not to have been fixed on the appellant insurance company.

As could be seen from the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and the documents, the Tribunal after considering all the facts and circumstances has come to the conclusion that the driver of the lorry was negligent and as such, liability has been fixed on him."

22. In another Judgment in the case of Renuka W/o Shekarappa Kathariki & others Vs The - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB Commandant, India Reserve Battalion Munirabad & others (MFA 102501/2015), this Court while dealing with similar situation, has held as under :-
"18.

entities.text: Renuka W/o Shekarappa Kathariki & others Vs The - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB Commandant, India Reserve Battalion Munirabad & others (MFA 102501/2015)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the Tribunal could not have denied the compensation.
Because involving of two vehicles composite negligence should have been examined by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the Government Insurance Department as well as insurance company of the lorry would be liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is only in case of the jeep driver this contingency would arise.
In this regard, the judgment of this Court dated 28.03.2019 in M.F.A.No. 24179/2012 and connected matters can be referred.

At paragraph 94 of the judgment reads as under:
"94. Section 122 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 deals with leaving vehicles in dangerous position.

It states that no person in charge of a motor vehicle shall cause or allow the vehicle or any trailer to be abandoned or to remain at rest on any public place in such a position or in such a condition or in such circumstances as to cause or likely to cause danger, obstruction or undue inconvenience to other users of the public place or to the passengers.

The owner of the vehicle has the right to driver the vehicle on the road and also - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB the right to part the vehicle, but the parking of the vehicle cannot cause any danger or obstruction to other passersby or passengers.
This is a restriction on the road to park the vehicle.

The aforesaid restriction on the road to part a vehicle is reasonable restriction and emanates from duty to take care."
23.
Therefore, a strict liability is cast on the person who parks his vehicle on the Highway.

It is important to note that, in the present case, had the driver of the lorry not parked the same on the middle of the road, probably the accident could not have occurred causing death of the rider of motorcycle and the petitioner sustaining grievous injuries.

It is in that context, we hold that the driver of the lorry was negligent and the entire negligence has to be saddled on the lorry driver only.
Similar is the view taken by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court (of which one of us is a member) in Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/
8

24. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case on hand and also keeping in mind the aforesaid decisions so also the provisions of IPC and Motor Vehicles Act and Motor Vehicle Rules,
we are of the considered opinion that the Tribunal has committed an error in fastening the liability to the extent of 50% on the deceased rider of the motorcycle.
Hence, we answer point No.1 in the negative.

Regarding Point No.2:
25.

Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioner has contended that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, aged about 41 years and earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing agricultural work.
Due the accident he has suffered permanent disability.
In order to substantiate the same, he has examined the Doctor as PW.2, who deposed that he has examined the petitioner and issued disability certificate as - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB per Ex.P7.
The said document discloses that petitioner has suffered permanent disability to an extent of 56% to his whole body.
Considering the nature of injuries and the disability, the Tribunal has taken the functional disability of petitioner at 35% which needs no interference.
26. The petitioner has not produced any documentary evidence with regard to his income.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2016, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.8,750/- p.m.
The petitioner was aged about 41 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '14' which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,14,500/- (Rs.8,750/- x 12 x 14 x 35%)
towards 'loss of future income'.
27.

Considering the nature of injuries, disability, period of treatment, it is just and proper to award - 21 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering as against Rs.40,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Towards medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,66,080/- on the basis of medical bills and documents produced by the petitioner.
The Tribunal has also awarded Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses.
The same left undisturbed.
29. Towards attendant charges, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.9,000/-.
The same is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
30. Considering the laid up period as three months, the loss of income during laid up period comes to Rs.26,250/- (Rs.8,750/- x 3 months) and the same is awarded.
31. The compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards food, nourishment and conveyance charges is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Considering the nature of injuries, avocation and long treatment of petitioner, it is just and proper to award Rs.1,00,000/-
under the said head.

Considering the evidence from both sides, the Tribunal has - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB held that the rider of the motorcycle was himself negligent by taking two pillion riders without wearing helmet violating the provisions of law and to that extent he has contributed to the accident and hence equally the rider of the motorcycle and driver of the lorry were responsible.

Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more pillion rider, may be a violation of the law.
But such violation by itself, without anything more,
cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence, unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
17. In the case on hand, the Tribunal has fastened the liability only to the extent of 50% on the driver of the lorry on the ground that the rider (deceased) of the motorcycle was carrying two pillions on the motorcycle by committing the offence punishable under Section 128 of M.V. Act.
In the instant case, the driver of the lorry has not taken any precautionary measures before parking the lorry in the middle of the road.
Even the owner or the lorry has not explained anything with regard to parking of the lorry in the middle of the road without following the Traffic Rules and Regulations.
A plain reading of Rule 15(2)(iv) & (x) of Road Regulations, 1989 makes it clear that driver of a motor vehicle shall not park his vehicle on the main road or one carrying fast traffic or where parking is prohibited.
Therefore, a strict liability is cast on the person who parks his vehicle on the Highway.
It is important to note that, in the present case, had the driver of the lorry not parked the same on the middle of the road, probably the accident could not have occurred causing death of the rider of motorcycle and the petitioner sustaining grievous injuries.
It is in that context, we hold that the driver of the lorry was negligent and the entire negligence has to be saddled on the lorry driver only.
Similar is the view taken by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court (of which one of us is a member) in Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/
